items.title: Warm-cluster settings

items.title: Sleeping clusters are labelled in the cluster list

items.title: A row budget across all connected clusters
items.summary: The browser now holds at most about 50,000 live rows across every connected cluster; past that, the least recently viewed cluster (never the active or a pinned one) goes to sleep and the engine drops its streams.

items.title: After a dropped connection (a laptop waking), the active and pinned clusters reconnect immediately; the rest still follow over about two seconds
Live tables redraw only the rows that changed
items.summary: When a stream update arrives, a resource table or the Pods table now re-renders just the rows whose object changed, instead of every visible row.

items.title: No more blanket 30 s refetch
items.summary: Pages no longer re-read CRD lists, RBAC, settings and similar data every 30 seconds while open; they refresh when you open the page, after an action, or on a cluster switch.

items.title: Only a few clusters stay streaming
items.summary: With many clusters connected, the engine now keeps at most 5 streaming (--warm-clusters or KUBEBAY_WARM_CLUSTERS, 0 for no limit, at most 50).

items.title: Tables are lighter on large clusters
items.summary: Moving the pointer over a row no longer redraws every visible row, and sorting a column reads each row's value once instead of once per comparison (about 38,000 reads down to 2,000 for 2,000 pods).

items.title: Pod Logs and Terminal open on the pod's default container
items.summary: A pod with a kubectl.kubernetes.io/default-container annotation now opens on that container instead of the first one (the same rule kubectl logs uses).

items.title: Apply to production?
items.summary: The YAML editor and Create Resource ask before applying to a cluster whose name reads like production (prod, prd, live, production), the same name check the terminal dock uses.

items.title: A chart's archive address is checked like a repository's
items.summary: A repository's index can name any URL for a chart archive; the engine now refuses a metadata, link-local or (in a cluster) loopback address and fetches the archive through the guarded transport, for chart pages, default values, install and…

items.title: Large kubeconfigs no longer load the machine
items.summary: The engine health check probes only connected clusters every 30 seconds; the others are checked when you open the Clusters page, at most every 5 minutes each and 10 at a time (so cloud login plugins are not run for every context).

items.title: Unapplied YAML edits are no longer dropped silently
items.summary: Closing a resource or pod drawer (Close, Esc, or a click on the page behind), changing its tab, or, on Create Resource, switching kind or following a link, now asks "Discard changes?" when the YAML was edited.

items.title: Star any resource
items.summary: Click the star after a name in a drawer, or choose Add to favorites in a table row's menu, for a pod, Deployment, Service, Ingress, any kind or custom resource.

items.title: CronJobs table shows a Status column
items.summary: Suspended, Active (jobs running) or Idle, with an Active Jobs count next to Last Schedule.

items.title: CronJobs table shows a Next Schedule column
items.summary: When the CronJob will next run ("in 12m", exact time on hover), honouring its time zone, and – when suspended or the schedule is invalid.

items.title: Favorites moved down the sidebar
items.summary: , just above Tools, as a collapsible section that remembers whether it is open.

items.title: Several windows in the desktop app

items.title: Pause and Unpause a KEDA ScaledObject
items.summary: From the KEDA page.

items.title: The Copy name button is larger
items.summary: And sits right after the name; the pod drawer's tabs scroll or wrap so no button is hidden.

items.title: Tables have no lines between rows
items.summary: The header keeps its underline, and rows are told apart by the hover tint and the selected tint with its accent bar.

items.title: A row's selection cell is the click target, not only the box in it
items.summary: Clicking anywhere in the cell around a row's checkbox ticks or unticks the row, and doesn't open the row's drawer.

items.title: Cluster icons in the left strip keep their real colour
items.summary: Clusters you weren't looking at were washed out to near grey; they are now only slightly muted.

items.title: Port forwards are reliable
items.summary: A local port can only be used by one forward at a time across every cluster.

items.title: The desktop app now updates itself
items.summary: Settings → Updates said "This build doesn't update itself", and for releases it was true: release.yml read the update public key only from a repository variable, so a key kept as a secret was ignored and the release shipped without an…

items.title: A Prometheus or Helm repo URL can't aim Kubebay at a cloud metadata service
items.summary: An address in the link-local range (169.254.0.0/16, where cloud nodes serve their credentials), the carrier-grade NAT range some clouds use, an unspecified or multicast address, or a URL with a user name and password is refused when you…

items.title: The UI is served under a Content-Security-Policy
items.summary: Scripts, styles, fonts, images, workers and connections may come only from the engine's own origin and its WebSocket; the theme script on the page is allowed by its SHA-256, and nothing may use eval or be framed.

items.title: A node shell can't outlive Kubebay
items.summary: The privileged helper pod is deleted when you close the drawer, but if the app or the browser died first nothing removed it.

items.title: CI actions are pinned to commits
items.summary: All 82 uses of a third-party GitHub Action in the workflows were floating tags or branches, including in the release workflow that holds the signing keys, so a moved tag would have run someone else's code there.

items.title: The macOS install script checks what it downloads
items.summary: Install-mac.sh compares the .dmg with the SHA-256 the release now publishes for each desktop installer, and with the release's cosign signature when cosign is installed, before it replaces the app or clears the quarantine flag.

items.title: The Helm chart gives the engine less
items.summary: The impersonation role and its binding are created only when OIDC is set, cover users and groups only (the engine never impersonates a service account), and can be narrowed to your IdP's groups with impersonation.groups.

items.title: Dependencies past six reachable vulnerabilities
items.summary: Go 1.26.11 (net/http, crypto/x509), go-tuf 2.4.1, DOMPurify 3.4.18 in the editor, React Router 7.18 and Astro 7.3.8 for the website, which now builds on Node 22.12.

items.title: A "What's new" window after every update
items.summary: The first launch after an update, manual or automatic, lists what changed in the release as a short list, once.

items.title: Prometheus is found by itself
items.summary: Kubebay looks for Prometheus in the cluster through the API server and fills the pod graphs without setup; a URL set in Settings still wins.

items.title: Favorites sit at the top of the sidebar
items.summary: In the same text size as the other links, and a cluster can be disconnected straight from the sidebar.

items.title: RBAC sections open and close
items.summary: , load only when opened, and a new Roles and their access list is searchable.

items.title: Pod logs in colour
items.summary: The Logs tab colours each line by its level, the way log tools do: errors red, warnings amber, success green, debug and trace dimmed.

items.title: The terminal lives in a dock under every page
items.summary: The local shell moves from its own page into a dock above the status bar, beside the sidebar, the way Freelens keeps it.

items.title: Releases carry the update signing key, so the desktop app can update itself
items.summary: An Update available button appears in the bottom-right corner when a newer version exists; it opens a popup with what changed, and Update now downloads, verifies and installs it.

items.title: ⌘K searches everything in a cluster
items.summary: Services, Ingresses, ConfigMaps, Secrets (names only), PVCs, ServiceAccounts, Roles, CronJobs, ReplicaSets and the other built-in kinds, custom resources (Argo Rollouts, Flux, KEDA, Karpenter, Gateway API, cert-manager), and the CRDs…

items.title: Switch cluster from ⌘K
items.summary: With the box empty it lists the clusters you used last; typing part of a name or alias finds one; switch prod, ctx stage or @stage puts clusters first.

items.title: ⌘K finds your objects, not just pods
items.summary: It searches the pods, Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, Jobs, nodes and namespaces of the current cluster, in groups by kind, ranked, and opens the one you pick (a pod in the Pods list with its drawer open).

items.title: An ⓘ on every page and insight card
items.summary: Beside each page's title, and each insight card's on Overview, RBAC and Cost / Waste, it says in a sentence what the page or card is and in another how it works, and links to that page of the user manual.

items.title: A Helm release opens on its Overview
items.summary: A release's drawer now opens on an Overview tab that shows

items.title: A user manual at kubebay.sardar.dev/docs
items.summary: 35 pages, one for each part of the app, written from the code.

items.title: Every vulnerability on one page
items.summary: A Vulnerabilities page, in the sidebar and the command palette, lists every workload Trivy-Operator found CVEs in, worst first, with its Critical, High, Medium and Low counts, how many have a fix, its images and when they were scanned.

items.title: Helm for someone who can see only some namespaces
items.summary: When your identity can't read Helm's release Secrets across the cluster, the Helm page lists the releases of the namespaces you picked, one namespace at a time, and says which of them it can't read ("You can't list Helm releases in…

items.title: Helm releases load when you connect, and stay live
items.summary: Kubebay streams the release Secrets' labels from the moment a cluster connects and fetches the release list in the background once there are releases, so the Helm page shows its rows at once (about 0.2 s after the click on 60 releases).

items.title: Click away to close a drawer
items.summary: A press anywhere on the page behind an open resource, pod or Helm drawer closes it, and a press on another row switches it to that row.

items.title: The namespaces you pick are kept
items.summary: Each cluster's namespace selection outlasts a reload and a restart, so the Pods, workload and other lists come back filtered as you left them, and an identity that can't list namespaces doesn't name them again.

items.title: Kubebay works for someone who can see only some namespaces
items.summary: When your identity can't list namespaces (a Rancher project member, a developer on a shared EKS, GKE or OpenShift cluster), the namespace picker starts in your kubeconfig context's namespace instead of a cluster-wide list that never loads.

items.summary: A new desktop smoke job builds the desktop app on windows-latest and ubuntu-22.04 the way the release does, launches it with KUBEBAY_SMOKE=1 (under Xvfb on Linux), and passes only if the engine sidecar starts and the web shell paints.

items.title: Air-gapped install bundle
items.summary: Each release gets kubebay-airgap-.tar.gz.

items.title: Installer sizes per release
items.summary: The release workflow weighs every installer and archive (.dmg, .exe, .msi, .deb, .rpm, .AppImage, .zip, .tar.gz) against the previous release's, matched by name with the version taken out, and writes the table to the job summary.

items.title: Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) tables
items.summary: A new "Devices (DRA)" sidebar group lists ResourceClaims (state as kubectl prints it: pending, allocated, allocated,reserved; the device classes asked for; the devices allocated as pool/device; the pods it's reserved for)…

items.title: Kubernetes 1.34 libraries
items.summary: Client-go and the other k8s.io modules move from v0.31.4 to v0.34.10, and Helm from v3.16.4 to v3.19.5, the newest that still build with Go 1.24.

items.title: Honest public claims
items.summary: The website's comparison table now comes from a typed data module (website/src/data/comparison.ts) in which every cell names its source and the day it was checked, and a website unit test (new website (astro) CI job, also run before each…

items.title: Extensions: your own columns and row actions
items.summary: ~/.kubebay/extensions.yaml adds table columns (a JSONPath per resource) and row-menu actions to any resource's table, Pods included.

items.title: StatefulSets and DaemonSets show their rollouts too
items.summary: Their drawers get the Summary line ("Revision 4, rolled out 3d ago · 2 rollouts in the last 7 days") from their ControllerRevisions, and a Rollout tab with each revision's ready pods.

items.title: Saved views
items.summary: Every resource table has "Save view", which keeps the table as you left it under a name: cluster, kind, namespaces, filter (the key:value filter language), columns and sort.

items.title: Signed releases with build provenance
items.summary: Release assets and the ghcr.io/rajasardar/kubebay image are signed keylessly with cosign (v2.6, by the release and publish workflows' GitHub identity) and carry GitHub build-provenance attestations.

items.title: Export a findings report
items.summary: The RBAC page's "Export report" saves every finding Kubebay's detectors have for the cluster as SARIF 2.1.0 (for code-scanning tools), JSON or Markdown.

items.title: Rancher-aware clusters
items.summary: A context that goes through Rancher's cluster proxy (https:///k8s/clusters/) gets a "Rancher" badge on the cluster list, whatever its name, and an "Open in Rancher" row action that opens that cluster in the Rancher dashboard.

items.title: Keyless image signatures are verified, and the signer is named
items.summary: The running-image signature check (RBAC page card and the workload, pod drawer Signatures tabs) now checks a keyless cosign signature the way cosign does against Sigstore's public instance, instead of leaving it to the admission controller.

items.title: When it last rolled out
items.summary: A Deployment's Summary tab says how old its current revision is and how many rollouts the last 7 days had, rollbacks included ("Revision 4, rolled out 3d ago · 2 rollouts in the last 7 days"), with a button to the Rollout tab.

items.title: Why a workload keeps breaking
items.summary: With history recording on, each broken hour now keeps its reason (CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled, ImagePullBackOff…), and after a recorded week the workload drawer's 7-day chip says so: "Broken in 9 of 166 recorded hours, on 5 of 7 recorded…

items.title: Assistants can propose changes; you approve them
items.summary: A new "Let assistants propose changes" setting under AI assistants (off by default) adds the MCP tools propose_change and get_proposal_status.

items.title: AI incident triage, step 2: Send
items.summary: When a key is set, the pod Triage tab's review pane has a "Send to " button that makes exactly the request shown, once, with the Anthropic Go SDK.

items.title: AI incident triage, step 1: consent and the review pane

items.title: Find AKS clusters
items.summary: The cluster list's Kubeconfig sources dialog also lists the AKS clusters your own az can see, in every resource group of the subscription you pick (az's current one first), and imports one with a click.

items.title: Find GKE clusters
items.summary: The cluster list's Kubeconfig sources dialog also lists the GKE clusters your own gcloud can see, in every location of the project you pick (gcloud's default first), and imports one with a click.

items.title: AI assistants (MCP)
items.summary: Settings → AI assistants lets Claude Desktop, Claude Code or another MCP client read the clusters you pick, whole clusters or named namespaces.

items.summary: The top five Needs attention rows show the worst pod's last log line (from the crashed run when it has restarted), and a workload's Summary tab shows its warnings over the last hour as 5-minute bars with whether they are new, started a…

items.title: Scale and restart from the table
items.summary: Deployment and StatefulSet rows get Scale… and Restart… in their row menu (DaemonSets get Restart…), each a small dialog that warns when Argo CD or Flux owns the workload and shows a policy rejection in place.

items.summary: A new helm loading icon and Spinner, shown while switching clusters; lists load as skeleton rows under their real headers, drawers as skeleton lines, lazily loaded pages as a skeleton page, and tables show a thin progress bar while cached…

items.title: The desktop window follows the theme

items.summary: The perf (kind) CI job now fails when the engine goes over a PRD §6 budget (cold start ≤ 1.5 s, idle RSS ≤ 150 MB, idle CPU ≤ 1%, 10k pods watched ≤ 400 MB), instead of warning.

items.summary: (was 1.24), which Helm 4 and the Kubernetes 1.37 libraries need.

items.summary: (was 1.22, out of support since February 2025).

items.title: Removed about 800 lines of unused styles and two unrouted pages (the old Home and Overview)
Every theme meets WCAG AA
items.summary: Text reads at 4.5:1 or better on every surface, status pills and button labels reach 4.5:1, and focus rings are solid and at least 3:1.

items.title: The shell renders every page header, toolbar input and select, keycap and sidebar link through @kubebay/ui, so the package is the single source of truth for that markup
Settings theme swatches match each theme's colours

Ghost and danger buttons match the design system everywhere (an app.css override had given them a weaker border and smaller text); the cluster picker's search, table, status and provider badges and row menu use the shared components…

items.title: Windows: no console window
items.summary: The app opened a black console window beside it, printed the engine's logs there, and closing it closed the app.

items.title: Less background work, so less battery
items.summary: Four causes

items.title: ⌘K now finds a custom resource's objects, not just its definition
items.summary: Typing scaled listed the CRDs (scaledobjects.keda.sh) but never your ScaledObjects, because their names don't contain the word.

items.title: ⌘K: cluster switching was hard to find, and two notes were wrong
items.summary: With the box empty, Switch cluster was listed below the page list, off screen; it is now first, with a hint line that never scrolls away.

items.title: A closed ⌘K palette no longer costs anything
items.summary: It was mounted for the whole session and kept its own full-object pod stream open on every page, with a second in-browser copy of every pod and a row rebuilt for each pod on every update, and it polled the cluster and port-forward lists…

items.title: A Secret's YAML no longer shows its values
items.summary: Opening a Secret in its drawer (the YAML tab and the summary) printed every value in plain base64, and its last-applied-configuration annotation held another copy.

items.title: The Overview no longer says "Healthy" before it has looked
items.summary: Right after you opened a cluster, Cluster health read Healthy · All 0 pods healthy and Needs attention Nothing needs attention for about two seconds, even on a cluster with crashing pods, because the page showed its verdict once any kind…

items.title: A Helm release's drawer never upgrades another release with its chart or values
items.summary: With one release open, opening another from the keyboard (Enter on its row) kept the first release's chart ref, version and edited values, so Save & upgrade would have installed them over the second.

items.title: Helm releases list about 10× faster
items.summary: Helm's list fetched and decoded every revision of every release before keeping the newest.

items.title: A drain that can't reach the cluster says why
items.summary: When Kubebay couldn't build a client from a cluster's credentials (a malformed certificate, say), Drain ignored the error, tried to cordon the node anyway and reported the cordon's failure.

items.title: Helm: no rendered Secrets in the release list
items.summary: The release list and history sent every release's rendered manifest to the page on each 12-second refresh, Secret data included, and nothing showed it.

items.title: Helm acts as you
items.summary: Helm read the kubeconfig itself instead of using the connection every other request uses, so it ignored the signed-in identity and, in in-cluster mode, which has no kubeconfig, couldn't work.

items.title: Helm release drawer stays current
items.summary: The drawer kept the release as it was when you clicked it, so after an upgrade, a rollback or a failure elsewhere its Rollback buttons pointed at the wrong revision.

items.title: The engine uses far less memory on big clusters
items.summary: Watching 100,000 pods, it held about 2 GB, five times the PRD's 400 MB budget, and grew while nothing changed.

items.title: The Overview's SPOF Radar and Service Health tabs load their data
items.summary: A stream that starts switched off (these tabs' PodDisruptionBudgets, Services, EndpointSlices, Ingresses and kube-system ConfigMaps open only when the tab does) never subscribed when it was switched on, so the tabs judged a cluster without…

items.title: Long tables scroll smoothly
items.summary: Scrolling the Pods table with 100,000 pods ran at about 37 frames a second in the performance harness.

items.title: A list filtered to several namespaces shows all of them
items.summary: Picking shop and payments showed only whichever namespace loaded last, because each namespace's rows replaced the others'.

items.title: The container image reports its version
items.summary: Kubebay --version and /api/version in the ghcr.io/rajasardar/kubebay image said dev.

items.title: The local terminal works in released desktop apps
items.summary: The release workflow built the desktop app's engine without the localshell build tag, so on macOS and Linux the terminal for your own machine said "local shell is not built into this binary" in every downloaded app; only make build builds…

items.title: Helm installs put every object in the release's namespace
items.summary: Installing or upgrading a chart from the Helm page put any object whose template has no namespace: into the kubeconfig context's namespace (usually default), while the release itself was recorded in the namespace you picked.

items.title: Kubebay no longer uses CPU while you're not doing anything
items.summary: With a cluster page open, the engine woke every open table's update queue 60 times a second whether or not anything had changed, about 5% of a CPU core on a quiet cluster.

items.title: Nothing loads from Google any more
items.summary: Every launch fetched a stylesheet from fonts.googleapis.com, for Inter (which nothing used) and JetBrains Mono (Display settings' third font), telling Google each time Kubebay opened; offline, JetBrains Mono quietly fell back to another…

items.title: The YAML editor works offline
items.summary: Every code editor (YAML tabs, Create resource, Helm values, the KEDA and right-sizing diffs) loaded Monaco from cdn.jsdelivr.net the first time it opened, so with no internet, behind a proxy that blocks it, or in an air-gapped install it…

items.title: Pages that can't read what they need say so too
items.summary: The Workloads Overview, Timeline, Right-sizing and Cost / Waste kept their loaders up forever when RBAC didn't let your identity list what they read.

items.title: A list you're not allowed to see says so
items.summary: When RBAC doesn't let your identity list a kind (say, Deployments across all namespaces), the page said nothing and showed a loading table forever, while the engine retried the list in the background.

items.title: A Deployment's Rollout tab finds its ReplicaSets again
items.summary: The drawer's copy of an object had its uid and creation time stripped like the YAML editor's, so the Rollout tab always said "No ReplicaSets found", the Timeline had no rollout revisions, and Summary's Created read "–".

items.title: Dialogs say what they are
items.summary: Modal takes a title, shown as the dialog's heading with a Close button beside it, and centred dialogs taller than the window scroll inside instead of running off it.

items.title: Configure Prometheus dialog
items.summary: The URL field, Cancel and Save show at once instead of waiting behind a spinner that never ended when the cluster's Services could not be listed.

items.title: Clusters page
items.summary: It no longer opens blank (HEADERS is not defined after the v0.5.0 version bump), and its row menu items work again.

items.title: Tables sorted counts as text, so a Job with 10 failures sorted below one with 9 (also Restarts, node Pods, event Count)
The Pods table mounted every row (5,000 pods meant 5,000 rows); it now renders only the rows in view, like the other tables
Pods' CPU and memory bars measured every pod against 1 core and 1 GiB, and memory was always drawn in the warning colour
Ages in tables went stale: a pod created "5s" ago still read "5s" a minute later, because rows only re-render when their data changes

Tables could stay on their loading skeleton forever on a fast cluster, and a table could briefly show another resource's rows (StatefulSets showing Deployments): stream frames were handled out of order
Pods never showed "live" and did not load CPU/memory on a second visit
The + button on resource tables did nothing; the row menu's "Edit YAML" opened the summary
The Create Resource dry-run toggle label used an undeclared colour token; it now uses the muted text colour
Every size, radius, animation duration and stacking layer in the app comes from the design tokens, so the command palette, context menus, drawers and dialogs always stack in the same order
Borders, focus halos, text colour and backgrounds missing in the Network Policy view, cluster picker and cluster detail drawer: six undefined --kb-* variables now point at real tokens (#12)
Cluster-picker nav highlight and engine-status dot follow the theme instead of fixed colours (#12)
ArgoCD sync and health pills had no background or border (their colour was built as invalid CSS)
Two notices styled with an info-banner class that had no CSS now render as proper banners
Light-theme users no longer see a dark frame on launch: the saved theme is applied before first paint
Text inputs and selects have a visible edge in every theme (3:1, WCAG 1.4.11) via a new --kb-border-control token; before, it measured 1.1–1.8:1
Focus rings, selected rows and status dots stay visible in Windows High Contrast (forced colours)
Full design-system audit across all 12 themes
